messages.subject: Redefining Matrices in Stan
parts:
Hey everyone,
I'll try and keep this concise, but I was just wondering if you can redefine matrices using a loop in Stan. This is related to an earlier post I made about unbalanced longitudinal data. 

Essentially, I have unbalanced and unequally spaced data (i.e. people showing up for a variable number of visits at various time points), and I'd like to define multivariate normal distribution for each individual's time points using an autoregressive covariance structure.One of the replies I received on my previous thread suggested storing the elements of each person's Sigma matrix in an array in column major order and then using to_matrix(), but since to_matrix returns a column (or row) vector, I am not seeing how this allows me to define different MVN distributions for each person. An example of what I would want to accomplish is something like this.

data{
  int<lower = 0> n // number of people in the dataset
  vec[n] n_recs // vector containing number of records for each person
 ...
}

model{
  for(i in 1:n){
    matrix[n_recs[i], n_recs[i]] Sigma // Here is the line of code that I'm curious about
    for(j in 1:n_recs[i]){
      for(k in j:nrecs[i]{
        ... // some loop to define the elements of the matrix
      }
    }
  }
}

I realize this might not be the most efficient way to code something like this up, but basically I'm just wondering whether it's even possible to redefine the dimensions of the matrix Sigma in each iteration of the loop. Thanks in advance for any help.
